english.title: Fail to comply with request of police officer or other authorised persons for fingerprints / photographs / both
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a person having given notification under section 9 of the Stalking Protection Act 2019, failed without reasonable excuse, when requested to do so by a police officer or authorised person, to allow that officer or person to

(A)_[take your fingerprints]_
(B)_[photograph a part of you]_
(C)_[take your fingerprints and photograph a part of you]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 10(5), 11(1)(a) and (2) of the Stalking Protection Act 2019.

english.notes:
(i) Persons under 18 can be charged with this offence.
(ii) A person who is subject to notification requirements must inform the police of all names and addresses used.
(iii) Notification must be done in a manner consistent with section 10 of the Act (different requirements exist for persons with a home address in England/Wales and those with addresses outside the geographical area).
(iv) When a person is already subject to notification requirements under Part 2 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003, reporting requirements under the Stalking Protection Act 2019 do not apply. Please see section 9(6) for further information.
(v) A person commits an offence on the day on which they first fail (without reasonable excuse) they to comply with the section and they continue to commit the offence throughout the period of which the failure continues. Despite this, persons will not be prosecuted more than once in respect of the same failure. See section 11.
(vi) Proceedings for an offence may be commenced in any court having jurisdiction in any place where the person charges with the offence resides or is found.

other.penalty:
Either way -Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
In relation to an offence committed before section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes into force, the reference to 12 months should be read as reference to 6 months imprisonment.
